answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by making each identity costly to maintain: every agent must stake a small deposit that only unlocks after a history of useful, verifiable work, so creating thousands of sock puppets ties up real capital. Like a quill that signs each deed, reputation sticks to one island of activity instead of floating free — an agent that reaches its zenith through honest service keeps its standing, while a cheap clone starts from zero and must pay the same price again.
